## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — polybuzz.ai serves the reporter's overlay ads from a page-owned full-document ad container, div#⁠character-chat-ad-layer, fed by the Venatus (hb.vntsm.com) and MGID loaders; with the reporter's own filters those loaders are already blocked on network-level platforms, so the overlay did not render in any live capture or rehearsal and apply_rule could not judge the element-hiding rule (inconclusive, baseline_symptom_absent). Candidate for maintainer review:⁠ polybuzz.ai#⁠#⁠.character-chat-ad-layer in BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt right after the existing polybuzz.ai#⁠#⁠.infeed-ad rule (line 4494) — the likely iOS gap is that Base's Venatus rule relies on $redirect, which Safari content blockers do not support.

## Candidate for review

`polybuzz.ai##.character-chat-ad-layer`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule came back environmentExperiment:⁠ inconclusive with errorKind baseline_symptom_absent and validationSkipped:⁠ true — under the reporter's own four filters (Base, Mobile Ads, Tracking Protection, Mail Tracking Protection) the Venatus (hb.vntsm.com, $redirect=noopjs) and MGID loaders are already stopped, so div#⁠character-chat-ad-layer stays empty and no overlay ad renders to compare in any phase; the candidate was never judged, i.e. an environment limit, not a rejected rule. The reporter (AdGuard for iOS) still sees the ads; per the compatibility guidance $redirect is unsupported by SafariConverterLib, so the rule that stops the Venatus SDK/loader on network-level platforms cannot act in the iOS app and its ads can be painted into that page-owned layer, where a content-blocker-supported element-hiding rule would still hide them. Unverified:⁠ no iOS execution model available, so neither the iOS gap nor the effect of hiding the layer could be observed.

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — dronexl.co serves its own anti-adblock gate:⁠ an inline detector writes `__adblocker=true` when https:⁠//ads.adthrive.com/abd/abd.js is not answered with 200, and a second inline script then injects the html-load.com recovery wall. The fix fits the existing shared adthrive/Raptive scriptlet group in BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt (lines 106 and 107, `set-cookie '__adblocker','false'` plus `prevent-xhr 'ads.adthrive.com'`), so add dronexl.co to every line of that group; the wall could not be validated because this CLI baseline answers the detector with a 200 noopjs redirect and the gate never appears.

`dronexl.co#%#//scriptlet('set-cookie', '__adblocker', 'false')`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

The reporter's iOS/Safari flow (which takes the `@@||ads.adthrive.com/abd/abd.js$xmlhttprequest` allowlist at line 103 instead of the redirect) cannot be reached from this environment, so the candidate was never judged.
